title: DXF SECTIONOBJECT late counts and bounded vertex pairing
status: bounded implementation with focused validation; no broad native-rendering claim
problem: SECTIONOBJECT group 92/93 currently clears already decoded section/back-line vertices. Moving each count after its otherwise unchanged complete vertex triples causes a successful native read with both arrays empty. A following typed write can therefore publish empty section geometry.
change: In dxfRW::processSectionObject only, locally track independent section and back-line vertex sequences and observe 92/93 as bounded counts while retaining their raw groups, without passing those counts to the destructive per-entity parseCode branch. Validate observed counts and unambiguous component pairing before any typed or raw callback. No public class layout, interface or protected direct parseCode behavior is changed.

authority.scope: SECTION defines group 92 as count of repeated 11/21/31 vertices, and 93 as count of repeated 12/22/32 back-line vertices.
DXF group order is not guaranteed.

producer_source: An in-tree authored SECTIONOBJECT with two section points and two back-line points was converted through ODA File Converter 27.1 to AC1027 DWG and back to DXF. The return contains 92=2 then two 11/21/31 triples and 93=2 then two 12/22/32 triples. The author tool moves only the two count groups in that ODA-returned record and creates an exact selected-record wrapper. The baseline probe returns read=1, verts=0, back=0; the candidate reports verts=2, back=2. Hashes bind source and projection; converter lineage is an observed manual join.
oda_controls: Controlled inputs derived from the authored source omit zero-valued 31/32, omit 92/93, or move those counts after their triples. ODA roundtrip preserves both arrays for omitted Z and emits explicit zero coordinates; it drops both arrays for the late-count and absent-count controls. This is an implementation observation, not a producer qualification of those alternate inputs. Existing native absent-count input remains supported by this candidate as requested.
pairing_and_admission: Each array has its own cursor, so interleaving the two arrays is accepted when each X anchors its Y and any Z. Y is required per point, Z may be omitted with default zero, and each coordinate must be finite. An observed count must occur once, be in [0,512] and match the final X count. Existing records with both no counts and complete coordinate pairs remain accepted. Newly refused cases include repeated or mismatched counts, missing or duplicate Y/Z, components before an X, grouped X values that cannot be paired safely, nonfinite coordinates, and counts/arrays above 512; several were previously silently misbound or normalized. Raw-only 411 opt-in also refuses these malformed arrays before callback rather than bypassing validation. Codes in 102 application groups and outside AcDbSection are unaffected.
validation: Fixture-free ASCII/Binary controls cover early, late and omitted counts, omitted Z, interleaved arrays, X/Y/Z and X/Z/Y component order within anchored points, copy/assignment, second-record isolation and the SECTION_OBJECT alias; application groups inside AcDbSection contain misleading count and coordinate codes; input 411 is exercised on valid arrays and malformed arrays under both default and raw-only policies. Failure controls cover both count mismatches, duplicate counts, 512/513 boundary, missing/duplicate components, unanchored/grouped coordinates, finite-value rejection and same-reader corrected retry, with no callbacks on malformed records. Successful typed re-emission/readback preserves geometry in ASCII and binary. Existing SECTIONOBJECT 411 and indicator-color reader/writer selectors pass, as does lc3_compat_check. Independent ezdxf 1.4.5 audit binds the exact ODA-source record reordering, selected projection, emitted geometry and ODA late/no-Z/no-count observations.
limits: The correction applies to the public dxfRW SECTIONOBJECT read path; an external subclass directly invoking protected parseCode is not covered.

No semantic claim is made for output rendering or full native CAD use; the selected ODA record includes proxy data and only its callback is qualified, while generated typed output controls use fixture-free records.
The source late-count projection and omitted-Z/count controls are explicitly edited inputs, not producer-authored alternate orders.
The separately hash-bound ODA conversion joins are manual session observations.
